The last verse of RV 10.121 answers the refrain with 'Prajāpati'; the Anukramaṇī names the deity Ka (Prajāpati).
AVŚ 10.7.17 joins knowing Brahman in man, the highest Brahman and Skambha.
The Atharvaveda's 'highest Brahman' is the nearest Saṃhitā use to the Upaniṣadic Brahman.
Bhartṛhari's 'Brahman as word' is a later philosophy of sound that draws on the Vedic exaltation of Vāc; the Saṃhitās do not use the term.
The Saṃhitās' immortality is chiefly full life and the immortal world of light; the Upaniṣads and Vedānta distinguish mokṣa from heavenly immortality. Recorded as contested.
The Mīmāṃsā treats heaven as the highest human end of ritual; the Upaniṣads and later schools hold heaven impermanent and distinct from liberation.
